blockbuilder-explorer.visual_critic_note: Deliberate dark theme with a proper CSS variable system, muted accent color (#4477AA), and uppercase panel labels show real design intent, but 6px panel gaps make the layout feel cramped and the force-graph renders as an illegible dense blue hairball at this size.
blockbuilder-explorer.encoding_integrity_note: Strong encoding integrity: scaleSqrt used correctly for node/color circle area, timeline Y-axis starts at zero with data-driven domain, all scale domains derived from d3.extent/d3.max; minor subset-relation issue where network node sizes rescale to filtered max (breaking invariant that remaining elements stay visually identical), and static SVG labels don't update with filter state.
flags: Update Storm (partial — CPU-side BitFilter.set + bitFilter.filtered() run synchronously O(n) on every brush mousemove, unthrottled, even though DOM/canvas renders are properly RAF-coalesced)
Stale Closure (minor — no window resize handler, so x/y scales inside brush closures become stale after resize)
blockbuilder-explorer.stress_test_note: Dirty-flag + RAF pattern correctly coalesces canvas redraws, no infinite loops or mid-flight transitions, pointer events unify mouse/touch cleanly, but the O(n) BitFilter computation executes synchronously on every mousemove frame before the RAF gate, leaving CPU-side update storm risk on large datasets.
blockbuilder-explorer.cognitive_load_note: Four linked crossfilter views (timeline, force network, color scatter, block list) are well-organized and the interaction model is coherent, but the force-layout network is a near-hairball with dense edges and 9px node labels that are unreadable at render size, creating a perceptual bottleneck at the dashboard's most analytical panel.
